name: cloudtrail_parse
description: Read AWS CloudTrail records offline (a file, a directory, gzip batches: Records files, arrays, single events, JSON Lines, lookup-events pages) one record at a time, and normalise each event with its identity, request, response and additional event data (access key id, source identity, shared event id, MFAUsed, eventVersion, requestID, addendum, tlsDetails and any other top-level key kept). `status` and `status_basis` say whether every record of every supplied file was read: a malformed line, a record that is not an event, a file that is not CloudTrail, a gzip that ends early (every record before the break is kept), an archive (.zip, tar: named, not read, so the read is partial), a next-page marker and files not reached before the time limit are counted, located (file, record, line) and listed; complete says nothing about what the account logged, and a digest file is named (digest_files) and read as no events. `session_origin` links an AssumedRole session to the successful AssumeRole-family calls in the records that could have issued it (the returned access key id, else the returned or request-derived session ARN; a call that returned a different access key id is disproved, and the session's creationDate narrows to calls within 5 seconds): a candidate with its basis, unresolved when several distinct calls match (listed up to a cap, with their count), not_found when none does; copies of one call (one eventID, or one sharedEventID with the same key or ARN, as in two exports or two accounts) count as one; never attribution to a person, and a failed call is never a source. Error codes are classified by name (a heuristic: authorisation_denied, authentication, throttling, validation, not_found, service); only authorisation denials are refusals. `identity` and `events` are matched against the text as it is printed, never against a withheld original; `identity` is a regex of at most 200 characters, a pattern that can take exponential time is refused, and one test of it that takes more than a quarter of a second fails the call, named. An argument the tool does not have is refused. NOT measured: what a trail recorded (a missing data event is not evidence nothing was read), digest-chain or log-file integrity (no validation is performed), whether a call took effect. SENSITIVE: a field named or shaped like a credential is withheld from every channel and its original written only with write_values, in a job, to a mode 0600 file under $OUT; other secrets are not recognised, so run it as a job with secret_output: true when requests may hold secrets. An out_file is never replaced by a smaller result: the earlier file is kept, the new one named beside it; a read that ended early publishes it as <name>.partial<ext> and names it partial_records or partial_events, never complete_*, and SIGTERM leaves no temporary file.

path.description: A CloudTrail file or a directory of them (.json, .json.gz, .gz, .jsonl, .ndjson; the shape is read from the content; an archive is named and not read)

events.description: Keep only these eventName values (exact, as printed)

identity.description: Case-insensitive regex (at most 200 characters) over the identity ARN or user name as printed; a pattern that can take exponential time is refused

errors_only.description: Only records that carry an error (an errorCode or errorMessage, or a failed ConsoleLogin response)

notable_only.description: Only the API calls this tool lists for a second look

link_sessions.description: Index the successful AssumeRole-family calls first (a second pass over the files, with a disk-backed index) and link each AssumedRole event to its candidate sources; default true

out_file.description: Optional JSONL path for every matching record, under the run directory (in a job, under $OUT: name it work/<your agent id>/..., which becomes $OUT). Never replaces a file already there: that one is kept and this one is named beside it

limit.description: Rows of each list returned inline (default 500, an inline page size); past it the whole list is in a file the answer names (under $OUT/tool-output in a job, work/<agent>/tool-output otherwise)

max_expanded_bytes.description: Most bytes read from one file after decompression (default 4 GiB); a file that reaches it is partial and says so

max_record_bytes.description: Most text held while one record is read (default 16 MiB); a larger record is rejected, located and listed, never cut

time_limit_seconds.description: Stop reading after this many seconds (default 540, at most 580); what was read is kept, the answer is partial and names the files not read

write_values.description: Write the originals of the values withheld from the answer to a mode 0600 file under $OUT. Honoured only when the tool runs as a job (run it with secret_output: true); outside a job it is refused and nothing is written
